pages.lesson:
LESSON: READING 3.4.1 INTENSIVE READING: POETRY

Grade: Grade 7
Subject: ENGLISH
Strand: Strand 3
Topic 3.4: Reading 3.4.1 Intensive Reading: Poetry

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! Today we learn about Reading 3.4.1 Intensive Reading: Poetry. Read the explanation, study the examples, do the practice, then try the revision quiz.

Big question: Why do people write poems?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. explain the structure of poems
2. read short poems addressing varied societal issues

SECTION 3: LEARN STEP BY STEP

1. explain the structure of poems
   In simple words: practise until you can explain the structure of poems. Use examples from school and home in Kenya.

2. read short poems addressing varied societal issues
   In simple words: practise until you can read short poems addressing varied societal issues. Use examples from school and home in Kenya.

SECTION 4: EXAMPLES

Example 1: Talk about Reading 3.4.1 Intensive Reading: Poetry using something you see at school in Kenya.

Example 2: Give a home example from your county, estate, or village.

Example 3: Teach a younger child one idea from this lesson in simple words.

SECTION 5: TRY THIS

1. Underline two new ideas about Reading 3.4.1 Intensive Reading: Poetry in the examples.
2. Explain Reading 3.4.1 Intensive Reading: Poetry to a parent using one local example.
3. Draw or write three things that show you understand Reading 3.4.1 Intensive Reading: Poetry.
4. Show that you can: explain the structure of poems

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (PRACTICE & REVISION)

1. Write five sentences about Reading 3.4.1 Intensive Reading: Poetry using examples from school or home.
2. Answer: Why is Reading 3.4.1 Intensive Reading: Poetry important for a Grade 7 learner?
3. Make a one-minute oral presentation to a parent or teacher.
4. List three ways you will practise this topic this week.

SECTION 7: CLASS ACTIVITY IDEAS

1. Read short poems addressing issues such as personal hygiene, HIV and AIDS, and COVID-19,
2. Study varied poems and present their different structures using graphic organisers,
3. Health Education is promoted as the learner tackles poems on issues such as personal hygiene, HIVand AIDS, and COVID-19

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. Why do people write poems?
2. What makes a poem interesting?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. explain the structure of poems
2. read short poems addressing varied societal issues

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open the Answers tab only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original learner lesson from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
